question: Using Table 2A-2, identify the characteristic background colors for temporary traffic control, incident management, and ETC-account-only signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 2A-2, temporary traffic control signs characteristically use a black legend on an orange background. Incident management signs use a black legend on an orange background, with fluorescent pink also shown as a background option. ETC-Account-Only signs use a purple background (with use of purple restricted per the provisions of Chapter 2F). Standards (mandatory): - For ETC Account-Only lanes/facilities, "Except for ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, if incorporated within the green background of a guide sign, the ETC pictograph shall be on a white rectangular or square panel set on a purple underlay panel with a white border. For rectangular ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, a white border shall be used at the outer edges of the purple rectangle to provide contrast between the pictograph and the sign background color." Options (permitted): - "Warning signs used for TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Guide signs used in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Detour signs in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Warning and guide signs used for TTC traffic incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background (see Figure 6O-1)." Support (informational): - "Common uses of sign colors are shown in Table 2A-2. Color schemes on specific signs are shown in the illustrations located in each applicable Chapter." Visual evidence: - [Image 4] Table 2A-2 shows the "Temporary Traffic Control" row with an orange background; the "Incident Management" row with orange and fluorescent pink backgrounds (black legend for both); and the "ETC-Account Only" row with a black legend and a purple background (footnote 5 notes purple is restricted per Chapter 2F). - [Image 2] Figure 6O-1 shows examples of traffic incident management area signs (warning, guide, and detour signs) rendered with black legends on fluorescent pink backgrounds. - [Image 3] Figure 2F-8 shows entrance guide signs for ETC Account-Only toll facilities using purple panels with the ETC pictograph and the ONLY message. - [Image 5] Shows a purple-background "Toll Pass ONLY" canopy sign identified as the ETC Account-Only lane example in Figure 2F-16. - [Image 7] Shows a temporary traffic control typical application (Figure 6P-12) with black-on-orange TTC warning signs such as W20-1 ROAD WORK AHEAD. Citations: - Table 2A-2 (p.43) - Section 2A.06 Support §3 (p.43) - Section 2F.03 Standard §2 (p.381) - Section 6H.01 Option §7 (p.798) - Section 6I.01 Option §4 (p.811) - Section 6I.02 Option §2 (p.811) - Section 6O.01 Option §10 (p.854) - Figure 6O-1 (p.855) - Figure 2F-8 (p.391)
gold_answer: Temporary traffic control: orange; incident management: fluorescent pink; ETC-account-only: purple.
